name: Citizenship by Birth in Territory or by Descent

requirements.blocker_text: Article 141 of Bolivia's 2009 Constitution: Bolivian nationality by birth is acquired by (a) birth within Bolivian territory (except children of foreign diplomatic personnel), or (b) birth abroad to a Bolivian mother or a Bolivian father -- explicitly gender-symmetric on its face, with no separate 'option at 18' or residence-establishment step required unlike some neighboring countries' constitutions (contrast Paraguay's Article 146, which requires the descent-route child to establish residence and formally elect nationality from age 18).
requirements.fix_path: Birth in Bolivian territory, or a documented parental link to a Bolivian mother or father, confers nationality automatically; obtain a Bolivian birth certificate or equivalent proof.

evidence_required.document: Birth certificate showing parental link or place of birth

sources.title: Lexivox (Bolivian legal-text repository, hosting the verbatim text of the 2009 Constitution) -- Article 141 on nationality by birth and descent

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Bolivia). STATUS: DRAFT -- the constitutional text itself was directly fetched and quoted from Lexivox, a Bolivian legal-database repository (tier 2, since it is not itself a .gob.bo domain, though it hosts verbatim primary legal text); Bolivia's own official gazette (gacetaoficialdebolivia.gob.bo) could not be reached (connection timeout) despite repeated attempts, and the OAS-hosted PDF returned a 403 error. GENUINE, POSITIVE STRUCTURAL FINDING: unlike several other countries built in this session (Iraq's asymmetric Articles 3/4, Afghanistan's disputed maternal-descent question), Bolivia's descent rule is explicitly gender-symmetric in the constitutional text itself, with no differential treatment between a Bolivian mother and a Bolivian father, and no additional option-at-majority step required. dual_citizenship_allowed set to true per Article 143 (confirmed via a tier-3 secondary source in this build, since the primary-text fetch captured Articles 141-142 but was truncated before reaching 143 -- flagged as a partial-primary-source situation rather than presented as fully tier-1/tier-2 confirmed).
